extracted.intended_audience: prospective ARIPO patent applicants, their agents/attorneys, and patent administrators in ARIPO Contracting States
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules and requirements for preparing, filing, prosecuting, and obtaining a patent under the Harare Protocol at the ARIPO Office (including fees, examinations, publication, grant, renewals, appeals, and conversion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents protect inventions, which are new, inventive and industrially applicable. An invention is a new solution to a technical problem and can be a product, process, apparatus or a new use of existing products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination requires the invention to have novelty, an inventive step and industrial applicability; if the application meets these requirements the Office proceeds to notify decision to grant, otherwise the applicant is invited to amend within a specified period or may face refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an ARIPO patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application consists of: a completed ARIPO Form 3 (Request Form); a description of the invention; one or more claims; one or more drawings (if any); an abstract; prescribed application fees or a written undertaking to lodge the fees; and designation of at least one state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed elements must be present for a correctly constituted application; missing elements can prevent according a filing date or lead to formality rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement for filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any language other than English, a translation of the document must be submitted within six months from the date of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file / representation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application may be filed by the applicant (inventor or assignee) or by an authorized representative (attorney, agent, or legal practitioner) with the right to represent the applicant before the national industrial property office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation is mandatory for applicants who are not resident or whose principal place of business is not situated in a contracting state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing routes and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application may be filed directly with the ARIPO Office or indirectly with the national industrial property office of any Contracting State acting as Receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application filed with a Receiving Office has the same effect as if filed at ARIPO on the same date. Filing may be done online, by personal delivery, email or registered mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO online service and incentive
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO provides an online service for filing, payments, notifications and tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online filing is available at eservice.aripo.org; the online filing option comes with a 20% reduction of the application fee. The service supports secure electronic conduct of ARIPO business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent documents filing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Any documents submitted by the applicant after transmittal of the application to the ARIPO Office must be filed directly with the ARIPO Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not send subsequent documents via the Receiving Office once the application has been transmitted to ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory requirements for according a filing date (examination on filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO Office checks that necessary information/documentation is provided so the application can be accorded a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application contains a completed application (request), a description and one or more claims, a filing date will be accorded and the applicant notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Formality examination covers certain formal aspects of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically checked items include the form and content of the application for registration, drawings and abstract, designation of the inventor, power of attorney, necessary translations, fees due, and technical and physical requirements of the description and claims. Noncompliance may lead to refusal but the applicant is afforded an opportunity to rectify deficiencies within prescribed time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination procedure and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office finds the application complies with formal requirements, it proceeds to substantive examination in accordance with the Harare Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination assesses novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability. If requirements are met, applicant and designated states are notified of the decision to grant; if they fail, the applicant is invited to amend within a specified period or the application may be refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to designated states and six-month objection period
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a decision to grant, each designated state is notified and should, within six months of the notification, make written communication to ARIPO expressing its objection or acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the expiration of the six-month period following communication of intention to grant, ARIPO will proceed to grant in respect of those designated states from which no written objection was received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal, amendment and rectification rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO Office may refuse an application for lack of compliance with prescribed formal or substantive requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In each case the applicant is afforded an opportunity to rectify deficiencies within prescribed time limits. The applicant may, within two months of the decision and on good grounds, request reconsideration. If refusal is maintained, the applicant may appeal or convert the application (see appeals/conversion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and conversion options
rubrics_metrics.description: Following refusal, the applicant can request the Office to reconsider; if still refused the applicant can appeal to the ARIPO Board of Appeal or request conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion may be requested within three months from the date of refusal to treat the application in any designated state as a national application under that state's law (or convert into an ARIPO utility model application). The decision of the Board of Appeal is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant, registration and certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the objection period, the Office will grant the patent for designated states with no objection, enter the patent on the Office’s register and issue a certificate of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant is made only for territories of designated states for which the grant was made; ARIPO publishes grant details in the ARIPO Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication content on grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant is published in the ARIPO Journal with details necessary for identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication includes owner’s details, inventor’s details, application number, patent number, designated states, any priority claims, title of the invention, class of the International Patent Classification, and the abstract accompanied by any drawings (if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and duration of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant has force and effect only with respect to territories of the designated states for which the patent grant was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cumulative duration of protection of an ARIPO patent is 20 years from the date of filing, subject to payment of annual maintenance fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual maintenance (renewal) fees — timing and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal fees are payable on an annual basis as indicated on the ARIPO schedule of fees and fall due on the eve of each anniversary of the date of filing, paid in advance to ARIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a six-month grace period for late payment which attracts surcharge fees. If the annual maintenance fee is not paid in accordance with the rule, the application (or patent) is deemed to have been withdrawn. ARIPO publishes notifications of renewed and lapsed applications and grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main fee schedule and chargeable extras
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected fees for patent services are specified (application, designation, renewal, grant/publication, extra claims/pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: application fee $250 (paper) / $200 (online); designation fee/state $75; renewal fee/state/year $40 (increments by $10 per year); grant & publication fee $600; $40 for each claim after the 10th; $15 for each page after the 30th. Regulations under the Harare Protocol contain the full list of fees.
